paragraphs.source_en: Each day he entered the castle, first paying his respects to Ieyasu, then visiting Hidetada and inquiring after Lady Gōyo, before carefully inspecting the fortifications. These inspections were not performed under orders; he wanted to discover any oversight that no one else had noticed. Destiny would not favor an idle man by deliberately opening a road for him to rise in the world. He understood Ieyasu's great ambition completely and devoted himself wholeheartedly to his service.

units.source_zh: 弥四郎仅仅为了做一区区大名，便背叛了家康，但长安无那般幼稚。

units.source_en: So long as he devoted himself to service, the rank of an ordinary daimyō would easily be within his reach.
units.source_zh: 只要他用心奉公，区区大名之位必不在话下。

paragraphs.source_zh: 家康心生戒备，旋又自责不已：我怎还对大贺弥四郎之事心有余悸？长安也知道弥四郎一事，他的才能和勤奋非弥四郎可比。弥四郎仅仅为了做一区区大名，便背叛了家康，但长安无那般幼稚。只要他用心奉公，区区大名之位必不在话下。

paragraphs.source_en: Perhaps the Buddha himself sent this man to assist me. Reaching this thought, Ieyasu reproached himself again—who in this world was not sent by the Buddha?

units.source_en: Perhaps the Buddha himself sent this man to assist me.
units.source_zh: 说不定乃是佛祖派他来助我。

units.source_en: Reaching this thought, Ieyasu reproached himself again—who in this world was not sent by the Buddha?
units.source_zh: 家康想到这里，又有些自责—在这个世上，何人不是佛祖所派？

paragraphs.source_zh: 说不定乃是佛祖派他来助我。家康想到这里，又有些自责—在这个世上，何人不是佛祖所派？

paragraphs.source_en: Jinnai was granted an entire street, where he opened a secondhand-clothing shop and resold the used garments he acquired. Unwilling to lose this privilege, he kept a strict watch over his subordinates.

units.source_en: Jinnai was granted an entire street, where he opened a secondhand-clothing shop and resold the used garments he acquired.
units.source_zh: 甚内得到了一条街，开了旧衣铺，将收来的旧衣转卖于人。

units.source_en: Unwilling to lose this privilege, he kept a strict watch over his subordinates.
units.source_zh: 他不想失去这个权力，遂严格监视下属。

paragraphs.source_zh: 甚内得到了一条街，开了旧衣铺，将收来的旧衣转卖于人。他不想失去这个权力，遂严格监视下属。

paragraphs.source_en: Once peace came to the realm, each person displayed his own talent, just as on the battlefield: one excelled with the spear, another at handling horses, and still others with the great sword or arquebus. Ōkubo Nagayasu possessed an extraordinary gift: he knew that every person had some use.

units.source_en: Once peace came to the realm, each person displayed his own talent, just as on the battlefield: one excelled with the spear, another at handling horses, and still others with the great sword or arquebus.
units.source_zh: 一到天下太平，人便会各显其能，与在战场上一样，有人擅耍枪，有些擅驱马，有人则长于大刀火枪。

units.source_en: Ōkubo Nagayasu possessed an extraordinary gift: he knew that every person had some use.
units.source_zh: 大久保长安拥有奇异的才能，他知人各有用。

paragraphs.source_zh: 一到天下太平，人便会各显其能，与在战场上一样，有人擅耍枪，有些擅驱马，有人则长于大刀火枪。大久保长安拥有奇异的才能，他知人各有用。

paragraphs.source_en: A great bell had originally stood within the castle, but because it was too close to Ieyasu's quarters, it was moved to the vicinity of Ishimachi, where the city's sole bell tower was erected. It was also Nagayasu who recommended Genpachi as bell-ringer—a former kasshiki acolyte of Kōfukuji in Nara whose religious name was Renshū—and who had Takiyama Yajibei of Honchō Second Ward cover his roof with tiles. The ringing of the Ishimachi bell became the hereditary duty of Genpachi's descendants, while the house of Takiyama Yajibei, the first to roof his home with tiles, immediately became one of Edo's sights.

units.source_en: A great bell had originally stood within the castle, but because it was too close to Ieyasu's quarters, it was moved to the vicinity of Ishimachi, where the city's sole bell tower was erected.
units.source_zh: 城中原有一口大钟，因为离家康居处甚近，便搬到了石町附近，在那里建了城内唯一的钟楼。

units.source_en: It was also Nagayasu who recommended Genpachi as bell-ringer—a former kasshiki acolyte of Kōfukuji in Nara whose religious name was Renshū—and who had Takiyama Yajibei of Honchō Second Ward cover his roof with tiles.
units.source_zh: 推荐曾是奈良兴福寺的喝食行者、法名莲宗的撞钟人源七的亦是长安，他还让本町二丁目的泷山弥次兵卫用瓦覆盖屋顶。

units.source_en: The ringing of the Ishimachi bell became the hereditary duty of Genpachi's descendants, while the house of Takiyama Yajibei, the first to roof his home with tiles, immediately became one of Edo's sights.
units.source_zh: 石町的撞钟由源七的子孙世袭，而首先用瓦盖屋顶的泷山弥次兵卫的家，也立刻成为江户一景。

paragraphs.source_zh: 城中原有一口大钟，因为离家康居处甚近，便搬到了石町附近，在那里建了城内唯一的钟楼。推荐曾是奈良兴福寺的喝食行者、法名莲宗的撞钟人源七的亦是长安，他还让本町二丁目的泷山弥次兵卫用瓦覆盖屋顶。石町的撞钟由源七的子孙世袭，而首先用瓦盖屋顶的泷山弥次兵卫的家，也立刻成为江户一景。

paragraphs.source_en: On the second day of the eleventh month in the sixth year of Keichō, a fire broke out at Kōnojō's house in Surugachō and spread into a great conflagration, causing immense damage. Thereafter thatched roofs were prohibited in the city and replaced with wooden shingles, yet no one thought of using roof tiles. But Yajibei roofed his house with tiles, and for a time crowds thronged before his door to marvel at the novelty.

units.source_en: On the second day of the eleventh month in the sixth year of Keichō, a fire broke out at Kōnojō's house in Surugachō and spread into a great conflagration, causing immense damage. Thereafter thatched roofs were prohibited in the city and replaced with wooden shingles, yet no one thought of using roof tiles.
units.source_zh: 庆长六年十一月初二，骏河町幸之丞家走水，大火蔓延，损失巨大，从此城中禁用茅草苫屋，改用木板，但谁也未想到瓦葺屋顶。

units.source_en: But Yajibei roofed his house with tiles, and for a time crowds thronged before his door to marvel at the novelty.
units.source_zh: 而弥次兵卫用瓦盖屋顶，因此他家门前一时人山人海，都来看新鲜。

paragraphs.source_zh: 庆长六年十一月初二，骏河町幸之丞家走水，大火蔓延，损失巨大，从此城中禁用茅草苫屋，改用木板，但谁也未想到瓦葺屋顶。而弥次兵卫用瓦盖屋顶，因此他家门前一时人山人海，都来看新鲜。

paragraphs.source_en: Thus Yajibei acquired the nickname “Half-Tiled Yajibei.” The story quickly spread throughout Edo, and before long many people began to imitate him.

units.source_en: Thus Yajibei acquired the nickname “Half-Tiled Yajibei.”
units.source_zh: 于是，弥次兵卫便有了一个诨名“半瓦弥次兵卫”。

units.source_en: The story quickly spread throughout Edo, and before long many people began to imitate him.

ja.t: がまねをするようになった。

units.source_zh: 事情迅速传遍江户，不久便有多人效仿。

paragraphs.source_zh: 于是，弥次兵卫便有了一个诨名“半瓦弥次兵卫”。事情迅速传遍江户，不久便有多人效仿。

paragraphs.source_en: People eagerly filled in low ground and applied for residential lots, yet no one wanted the corner plots along the streets. Such places were at risk of visits from thieves, and their outer walls and watchtowers also increased the expense. On learning this, Nagayasu immediately proposed to Hidetada, “My lord, what would you say to this: grant the privilege of an audience to anyone willing to establish his home on an outlying corner?”

units.source_en: People eagerly filled in low ground and applied for residential lots, yet no one wanted the corner plots along the streets.
units.source_zh: 人们纷纷填充洼处，请封宅地，却无人愿意要街市拐角处。

units.source_en: Such places were at risk of visits from thieves, and their outer walls and watchtowers also increased the expense.

ja.t: もかさんだからである。

units.source_zh: 这等地方既有被盗贼光顾之险，费用也会因为外墙和望楼而增加。

units.source_en: On learning this, Nagayasu immediately proposed to Hidetada, “My lord, what would you say to this: grant the privilege of an audience to anyone willing to establish his home on an outlying corner?”

ja.t: 、このようになさってはいかがでしょう。

units.source_zh: 得知此事，长安马上向秀忠建议：“大人看这样如何：愿意安家在僻角处的人特许谒见。”

paragraphs.source_zh: 人们纷纷填充洼处，请封宅地，却无人愿意要街市拐角处。这等地方既有被盗贼光顾之险，费用也会因为外墙和望楼而增加。得知此事，长安马上向秀忠建议：“大人看这样如何：愿意安家在僻角处的人特许谒见。”

paragraphs.source_en: “The privilege of an audience?”

units.source_en: “The privilege of an audience?”
units.source_zh: “特许谒见？”

paragraphs.source_zh: “特许谒见？”

paragraphs.source_en: “Then, to enhance their prestige, they will vie with one another to settle in those outlying places. If those places remain vacant, the town will look desolate, and that must never be allowed.”

units.source_en: “Then, to enhance their prestige, they will vie with one another to settle in those outlying places.
units.source_zh: “如此，他们为提高威望，便会争相把家安于僻处。

units.source_en: If those places remain vacant, the town will look desolate, and that must never be allowed.”
units.source_zh: 那些地方若是空地，城镇看起来便显荒芜，那断断不可。”

paragraphs.source_zh: “如此，他们为提高威望，便会争相把家安于僻处。那些地方若是空地，城镇看起来便显荒芜，那断断不可。”

paragraphs.source_en: In truth, Nagayasu himself derived boundless pleasure from all this. Building castles and digging ponds is in my very nature, he thought.

units.source_en: In truth, Nagayasu himself derived boundless pleasure from all this.
units.source_zh: 实际上，长安自己也从此中得到了无限乐趣。

units.source_en: Building castles and digging ponds is in my very nature, he thought.
units.source_zh: 筑城建池乃我的天性，他这般想。

paragraphs.source_zh: 实际上，长安自己也从此中得到了无限乐趣。筑城建池乃我的天性，他这般想。

paragraphs.source_en: But did he possess the ability to shape human talent?

units.source_en: But did he possess the ability to shape human talent?
units.source_zh: 但他有无塑造人才的能耐呢？

paragraphs.source_zh: 但他有无塑造人才的能耐呢？

paragraphs.source_en: After gaining Hidetada's trust, Nagayasu secured for Tadateru a large site on the banks of the Asakusa River on which to build a residence. Until then, Tadateru had lived with his mother in Sunpu and had not yet visited his own domain of Kawanakajima.

units.source_en: After gaining Hidetada's trust, Nagayasu secured for Tadateru a large site on the banks of the Asakusa River on which to build a residence.
units.source_zh: 在得到秀忠的信任之后，长安为忠辉在浅草河岸请封了一块大大的建府之地。

units.source_en: Until then, Tadateru had lived with his mother in Sunpu and had not yet visited his own domain of Kawanakajima.
units.source_zh: 在此之前，忠辉一直和母亲同住于骏府，还没去过自己的领地川中岛。

paragraphs.source_zh: 在得到秀忠的信任之后，长安为忠辉在浅草河岸请封了一块大大的建府之地。在此之前，忠辉一直和母亲同住于骏府，还没去过自己的领地川中岛。

paragraphs.source_en: From the plan of the castle and the development of new rice fields to roads and bridges, everything seemed to convey Ieyasu's true intentions, while Nagayasu employed all his skills and directed the people.

units.source_en: From the plan of the castle and the development of new rice fields to roads and bridges, everything seemed to convey Ieyasu's true intentions, while Nagayasu employed all his skills and directed the people.

ja.t: えているかのようであり、

units.source_zh: 从城池格局、新田开发到道路桥梁，一切都似在传达家康的真意—长安运用他所长所能，指挥众人。

paragraphs.source_zh: 从城池格局、新田开发到道路桥梁，一切都似在传达家康的真意—长安运用他所长所能，指挥众人。

paragraphs.source_en: As Ieyasu's sixth son, Tadateru would soon be granted an official rank—at least that of Junior Fourth Rank and Provisional Minor Captain of the Left Division of the Inner Palace Guards—and would also receive land for a residence below Edo Castle.

units.source_en: As Ieyasu's sixth son, Tadateru would soon be granted an official rank—at least that of Junior Fourth Rank and Provisional Minor Captain of the Left Division of the Inner Palace Guards—and would also receive land for a residence below Edo Castle.
units.source_zh: 忠辉既为家康六子，不久便当被委以官职，至少当是从四品的左近卫权少将，亦会在江户城下获赐府宅之地。

paragraphs.source_zh: 忠辉既为家康六子，不久便当被委以官职，至少当是从四品的左近卫权少将，亦会在江户城下获赐府宅之地。

paragraphs.source_en: As Nagayasu watched Edo changing before his eyes, his thoughts gradually wandered: How should he train Tadateru? He often recalled Hideyori, who was about Tadateru's age, and the gold ingots he had seen at Osaka Castle; his heart burned within him.

units.source_en: As Nagayasu watched Edo changing before his eyes, his thoughts gradually wandered: How should he train Tadateru?
units.source_zh: 长安看到变化的江户，渐渐神驰：应如何调教忠辉？

units.source_en: He often recalled Hideyori, who was about Tadateru's age, and the gold ingots he had seen at Osaka Castle; his heart burned within him.
units.source_zh: 他常常想起和忠辉差不多大小的秀赖，想起在大坂城看到的金块，他的心在燃烧。

paragraphs.source_zh: 长安看到变化的江户，渐渐神驰：应如何调教忠辉？他常常想起和忠辉差不多大小的秀赖，想起在大坂城看到的金块，他的心在燃烧。

paragraphs.source_en: Hideyori was the Taikō's son, while Tadateru was Ieyasu's heir; and he, Ōkubo Nagayasu, possessed a special gift for discovering and mining gold. It was precisely for these reasons that he could not put that gold out of his mind.

units.source_en: Hideyori was the Taikō's son, while Tadateru was Ieyasu's heir; and he, Ōkubo Nagayasu, possessed a special gift for discovering and mining gold.
units.source_zh: 秀赖乃太阁之子，而忠辉为家康之后，他大久保长安拥有探掘金矿的特殊本事。

units.source_en: It was precisely for these reasons that he could not put that gold out of his mind.
units.source_zh: 正是因为这些缘故，他才对那黄金念念不忘。

paragraphs.source_zh: 秀赖乃太阁之子，而忠辉为家康之后，他大久保长安拥有探掘金矿的特殊本事。正是因为这些缘故，他才对那黄金念念不忘。

paragraphs.source_en: First he must carefully cultivate Tadateru and make him surpass Hideyori, though Nagayasu had not yet fully resolved to do so. Perhaps every human heart harbors a vague yet eternal desire for conquest; so it was with Nagayasu.

units.source_en: First he must carefully cultivate Tadateru and make him surpass Hideyori, though Nagayasu had not yet fully resolved to do so.

ja.t: えさせねばならない。ただ、
めきってはいなかった。

units.source_zh: 首先得好生培养忠辉，让他超过秀赖，只是长安尚未下定决心。

units.source_en: Perhaps every human heart harbors a vague yet eternal desire for conquest; so it was with Nagayasu.
units.source_zh: 或许，人人心中皆有一种模糊而永恒的征服之念，长安即是如此。

paragraphs.source_zh: 首先得好生培养忠辉，让他超过秀赖，只是长安尚未下定决心。或许，人人心中皆有一种模糊而永恒的征服之念，长安即是如此。

paragraphs.source_en: Tadateru's betrothal had already been arranged; his intended bride was Irohahime, daughter of Date Masamune of Ōshū. The match had been settled in the fourth year of Keichō. The intermediary was the tea master Imai Sōkun. Nagayasu understood perfectly well that this was merely a bargain struck by the two fathers for the sake of their own futures.

units.source_en: Tadateru's betrothal had already been arranged; his intended bride was Irohahime, daughter of Date Masamune of Ōshū.
units.source_zh: 忠辉的婚约已定，女方为奥州伊达政宗之女五郎八姬。

units.source_en: The match had been settled in the fourth year of Keichō.
units.source_zh: 此事庆长四年便已确定。

units.source_en: The intermediary was the tea master Imai Sōkun.
units.source_zh: 媒人为茶人今井宗薰。

units.source_en: Nagayasu understood perfectly well that this was merely a bargain struck by the two fathers for the sake of their own futures.

ja.t: にすぎないことが、よくわかっていた。

units.source_zh: 长安心中甚是清楚，这不过两方父亲为自己的未来而做的一笔交易。

paragraphs.source_zh: 忠辉的婚约已定，女方为奥州伊达政宗之女五郎八姬。此事庆长四年便已确定。媒人为茶人今井宗薰。长安心中甚是清楚，这不过两方父亲为自己的未来而做的一笔交易。
